newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 1.73 pct lower on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 1.73 pct lower on rumours.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks ended 1.73 percent lower on Thursday after investors sold property, finance and bank stocks on rumours that a property developing firm was facing cash problems, brokers said.
The SET index, which fluctuated frequently during the morning session, declined 16.44 points to 933.00 at the close. Total turnover was 5.3 billion baht.
"The market sentiment was poor today on rumours that a property firm was having cash problems. The rumours induced investors to sell property stocks," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
Thursday's close was at the lowest level in more than three years.
The market retreated sharply after rumours spread in the market that Somprasong Land Plc was having cash problems and was in difficult position to settle its debts owed to some finance companies.
Prasong Panichpakdi, managing director of Somprasong Land, told Reuters that the rumours were not true.
"How could the company have financial problems as it has total assets of more than nine billion baht ($360 million) now," Prasong said.

The rumours caused all major sectors on the board to tumble. The finance sector fell most as it slipped 6.79 percent followed by the property sector, which declined 3.88 percent, and the banking sector, which shed 2.66 percent.

Large capitalised Finance One topped the list of most active stocks in terms of value, falling seven baht to 77.50. Siam Commercial Bank declined eight to 202 and Somprasong Land dropped 1.25 to 12.50.
Support is seen by some brokers at around 920-point on Friday while resistance is at 950.
